posts.title: ICE separates families in the interior, labels the kids unaccompanied
posts.excerpt: A new Mother Jones investigation finds ICE separating children from their parents in the country's interior and deeming them unaccompanied, routing kids who have families into ORR custody. Attorneys…
posts.body: A new Mother Jones investigation finds ICE separating children from their parents in the country's interior and deeming them unaccompanied, routing kids who have families into [ORR custody](https://www.muellershewrote.com/p/headlines-for-october-14-2026). Attorneys interviewed for the piece say kids picked up far from the border made up about one in five ORR referrals between July 2025 and May 2026, against 3 to 5% under past administrations, with the figures detailed in [an Oct 6 petition](https://www.change.org/p/stop-separating-immigrant-children-from-their-parents-and-bring-them-home).

posts.title: A calm heart the night before is tied to faster marathon times
posts.excerpt: Published Oct 14, 2026, 7:00 AM: Of the 73 male marathoners tracked with a single-lead ECG patch the night before the 2025 Padua Marathon, those with a lower minimum sleeping heart rate and stronger…
posts.body: Published Oct 14, 2026, 7:00 AM: Of the 73 male marathoners tracked with a single-lead ECG patch the night before the 2025 Padua Marathon, those with a lower minimum sleeping heart rate and stronger vagal modulation finished faster the next day, independent of age, BMI, and training hours, [per the Oct 12 study in Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/cardiovascular-medicine/articles/10.3389/fcvm.2026.1932814/full). The authors read the pattern as a readiness signal: stronger vagal tone overnight may mark more restorative sleep, and that recovery is the preparedness that shows up the next morning.

posts.title: Chainguard puts CI checks inside the agent loop
posts.excerpt: Published Oct 14, 2026, 4:25 AM: Chainguard announced Checks on Wednesday, a verification engine that pulls CI out of its old spot after the pull request and runs it inside the agent's working loop,…
posts.body: Published Oct 14, 2026, 4:25 AM: Chainguard announced Checks on Wednesday, a verification engine that pulls CI out of its old spot after the pull request and runs it inside the agent's working loop, delivering signed, trusted verification in seconds, per its [PR Newswire release](https://www.morningstar.com/news/pr-newswire/20261014ne71672/introducing-chainguard-checks-reinventing-continuous-integration-for-the-agentic-era). Every passing run produces a signed attestation tying together the environment, test result, and commit, so a merge gate can verify it and merge without re-running the test suite.

posts.title: No clear link between load and fiber-type muscle growth
posts.excerpt: Across eight muscle-biopsy studies, every comparison of training load against fiber-type growth saw its confidence interval cross zero, per a Frontiers in Physiology meta-regression. The authors call…
posts.body: Across eight muscle-biopsy studies, every comparison of training load against fiber-type growth saw its confidence interval cross zero, [per a Frontiers in Physiology meta-regression](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2026.1953601/full). The authors call the fiber-specific trend preliminary: too few studies and wide intervals to build a program on.

posts.title: Decision models cut AI agent token costs
posts.excerpt: A new class of "decision models" trims an AI agent's toolset to the few tools that fit each request, returning a calibrated choice plus a confidence score with no generated text and no embeddings or…
posts.body: A new class of "decision models" trims an AI agent's toolset to the few tools that fit each request, returning a calibrated choice plus a confidence score with no generated text and no embeddings or index. [In the author's benchmark](https://dev.to/aws/cut-ai-agent-token-costs-with-decision-models-for-tool-selection-2320), selecting first matched the right tool on every query while cutting chat tokens by roughly two-thirds.

posts.title: Endurance tests aren't interchangeable
posts.excerpt: In 186 fit young adults, a shared endurance factor explained only about 60 to 70% of scores across six standard endurance tests, with running tests clustering together and rowing tests clustering…
posts.body: In 186 fit young adults, a shared endurance factor explained only about 60 to 70% of scores across six standard endurance tests, with running tests clustering together and rowing tests clustering together instead, [per an October 1 study in Frontiers in Physiology](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2026.1973746/full). Rowing performance leaned on strength and power, especially upper-body, so a 12-minute row is no stand-in for a 12-minute run when the question is where your running fitness stands.

posts.title: Chicago names former officer suspect in 1960 killing of 8-year-old
posts.excerpt: Chicago police say former officer Thomas Francis McInerney abducted and killed 8-year-old Gloria Kowalewicz as she walked to church in November 1960. The case sat unsolved for 65 years until…
posts.body:
Chicago police say former officer Thomas Francis McInerney abducted and killed 8-year-old Gloria Kowalewicz as she walked to church in November 1960.
The case sat unsolved for 65 years until investigators submitted her preserved coat to the FBI for [genetic genealogy](https://wegotthiscovered.com/true-crime/65-years-later-chicago-police-name-their-own-officer-as-suspect-in-8-year-olds-killing/), which led them to McInerney's family tree.

posts.body: Robert E. Hall of Stanford and Michael Woodford of Columbia [won the 2026 Nobel economics prize](https://www.khsu.org/2026-10-12/two-americans-win-nobel-prize-in-economics-for-work-on-boom-bust-cycles) for the "microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation." posts.body: Version 2.03 of the PS5SX2 emulator has been free on GitHub since October 11, adding experimental external USB drive support, per [Notebookcheck](https://www.notebookcheck.net/PS5-can-now-play-original-PS2-discs-but-there-s-a-catch.1421922.0.html). When a user asked whether PS3 discs would play on the PS5 too, developer Sword answered: "It will."

posts.title: Stopping sets early beats grinding for jump and sprint
posts.excerpt: A Frontiers in Physiology meta-analysis of 12 randomized controlled trials, published October 6, found that stopping sets when rep speed dipped about 10% produced better jump and sprint gains than…
posts.body: A [Frontiers in Physiology meta-analysis](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/physiology/articles/10.3389/fphys.2026.1893020/full) of 12 randomized controlled trials, published October 6, found that stopping sets when rep speed dipped about 10% produced better jump and sprint gains than pushing through to 30-40% velocity loss. The 10%-loss group added 9.2% to countermovement jump against 5.4% for the 30%-loss group, while doing less than half the total reps.

posts.body: On Monday, HCLTech signed a Global Premier Partnership with Anthropic to bring agentic AI to large enterprises. Its services teams will build industry solutions on Claude, Cowork, and Claude Code, per [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/india/indias-hcltech-signs-pact-with-anthropic-set-up-business-unit-2026-10-12/).

posts.title: Columbus Day closes federal offices, banks, and mail today
posts.excerpt: The closures come with exceptions: USPS is holding regular mail while Priority Mail Express still moves, and most bank branches are shut with ATMs and apps as the workaround, per El Cronista's…
posts.body: The closures come with exceptions: USPS is holding regular mail while Priority Mail Express still moves, and most bank branches are shut with ATMs and apps as the workaround, per [El Cronista's holiday guide](https://www.cronista.com/en/today/work-calendar-this-monday-october-12-is-a-federal-holiday-and-there-will-be-a-long-weekend-for-public-offices-and-banks-in-the-united-states/). Wall Street, big retailers, and UPS and FedEx all run normally.
